During the course of the hearing, the representative of the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that in terms of the direction of the Commission vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 22.4.2025, CTUIL has already filed its compliance affidavit on 16.5.2025. Learned counsel for the OPTCL submitted that OPTCL has also filed its compliance affidavits in these matters. Learned counsel further submitted that OPTCL has raised an apprehension of some delay in the implementation of its S/S owing to land acquisition issues. Learned counsel further submitted that while OPTCL is trying to complete the Project in time, in case of unavoidable delay in the implementation of the said S/s, a dispensation as available to the TSP (i.e. extension/ grace period of 180 days on account of Force Majeure events) ought to also be extended to OPTCL. The Respondent, Bihar State Power Holding Company Limited (BSPHCL), submitted that, insofar as issues with respect to time overrun and cost overrun are concerned, the Commission may observe that these issues would be adjudged on their own merits as and when they arise. The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that in accordance with the direction of the Commission, the Petitioners have impleaded the Bulk Consumers, as conveyed by CTUIL, in the said matters and filed the amended memo of the parties. However, CTUIL has once again revised the list of Bulk Consumers, and in view of this, the Petitioner will have to again file a revised memo of parties in these matters. In this regard, the representative of CTUIL clarified that, upon processing the various applications received on a month-to-month basis, the names of applicants who do not meet the requisite criteria are struck off the list, which has led to the revision of the list of Bulk Consumers in this case. Considering the submissions of the parties in the matters, the Commission directed that the Petitioner to file a revised memo of the parties, if required. # ** Corrigendum to RoP in Petition No. 513/TL/2024 of the Hearing dated 07.07.2025: ** 22. However, subsequently, a corrigendum to the ROP dated 14.07.2025 was issued wherein CTUIL and Petitioner were directed to submit the following information: a) The Petitioner had filed an affidavit on 03.07.2025, placing on record the details of meetings which were held on 17.03.2025 and 09.05.2025 in the presence of representatives of the CEA, MNRE, ERPC, CTUIL, OPTCL, GRIDCO, the Petitioner, and Green Hydrogen/ Ammonia Developers, wherein suggestions were made to shift the proposed 765/400 kV Gopalpur substation closer to the Tata Steel SEZ and modalities for sharing additional costs were discussed. However, due to a lack of consensus between the parties, the Petitioner is not shifting the substation. b) There is no change in the location of the sub-station, and it remains the same, as proposed. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that pursuant to the direction of the Commission vide Record of Proceedings (‘RoP’) for the hearing dated 7.7.2025, the Petitioner has filed its compliance affidavit dated 10.9.2025. The representative of the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that vide RoP dated 7.7.2025, CTUIL, along with the Petitioner, was directed to file certain information by way of an affidavit. However, CTUIL has no further submissions to make in the matter. Considering the submissions made by the learned senior counsel and representative of the parties, the Commission reserved the matter for Order. Accordingly, we direct the Petitioner and the CTUIL to approach the NCT with the observations as made in this Order. After the decision of the NCT, the Petitioner is granted liberty to approach the Commission, if so advised.
